newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAILEY EAGER TO BOUNCE BACK WITH NEW RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY EAGER TO BOUNCE BACK WITH NEW RECORD.

text.p: Olympic champion Donovan Bailey, defeated by Maurice Greene in Sunday's world 100 metres final, will seek compensation by further reducing his own world record this season.
"Get healthy again and lower my record before the end of the season is what I intend to do now," said Bailey, who set the current mark of 9.84 seconds at last year's Atlanta Olympics.

Canadian Bailey, troubled by cramps on Saturday, had to settle for second place with 9.91 behind American champion Greene, who won in 9.86. Only Bailey himself and American Leroy Burrell have ever run faster.

"I've been hurt for the last while," said Bailey. "I've lost 12 pounds (five kg) since I last competed in Europe. Yesterday (Saturday) was a struggle but I don't want to get into that. I'm not going to sit here and make excuses. I was second."
Pre-race favourite Ato Boldon, who clocked 9.87 in Saturday's second round before finishing a disappointing fifth on Sunday, also has designs on the world record.
"I was suffering with cramps before the race," said the Trinidadian extrovert. "I've still got another chance, I've got to keep my head on straight for the 200."

Boldon always knew Greene would be a major threat. When Greene joined John Smith's training camp in California in September last year, he lived with Boldon for some time and upset his host by watching videos of his races and correcting his mistakes.
Boldon said before the championships started that if his talent caught up with his ego, he would run 9.69. Bailey did not give a target.
The pair will need to move fast to beat Greene to the record.
"The world record will have to come," Greene said. "Today, it could not be broken but it will be. That's my next goal."
